### AI, in simple words
**AI** is software that does tasks that normally need human-like thinking—such as understanding words, spotting images, or making predictions. **Machine learning (ML)** is a kind of AI that learns patterns from examples instead of being given a rule for every situation.

**Easy ML types (from IBM):**
- **Supervised learning:** learns from examples with answers—like emails marked “spam” or “not spam.”
- **Unsupervised learning:** groups similar things without answers already attached—like finding groups of similar customers.
- **Reinforcement learning:** learns by rewards and penalties—like learning which move helps win a game.

IBM also lists self-supervised and semi-supervised learning. [IBM: Types of Machine Learning](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/machine-learning-types)

**Microsoft Copilot** is an AI assistant in Microsoft 365. It can help draft content, find information, summarize documents, emails, and meetings, analyze data, and answer questions. It works with apps including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams. [Microsoft Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/solutions/individuals)

**Real chip-news example:** A report on Intel’s upcoming Granite Rapids-WS workstation chip says it appeared with **86 cores and 172 threads**, aimed at competing with AMD Ryzen Threadripper/Threadripper Pro systems. Think of cores as many workers inside one computer: more capable workers and fast access to memory can help with demanding jobs such as running AI models, processing large data, 3D work, and engineering simulations. Powerful chips matter because AI must perform huge numbers of calculations; better hardware can make that work faster and allow bigger tasks to run locally. [News report](https://www.techpowerup.com/341448/intel-granite-rapids-ws-appears-with-86-cores-and-172-threads-built-for-hedt)
